what: OCADE chat answer quality against the local engine on this machine
limits: Proves what the engine answers through the production streaming path. Proves nothing about the authenticated browser UI, which requires a signed-in session and is evidenced separately.
engineConfiguration: These figures are only meaningful against an engine launched with OCADE's resource ceilings (OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=1, OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1, a short OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE). Measured against a hand-started runtime holding two models at once — 5.53 GB and 5.40 GB on a 15.65 GB machine — the long-document step failed three times at exactly the transport's 300-second limit, because the system was swapping rather than because the model could not answer.

machine.gpu: Integrated graphics only (Parsec Virtual Display Adapter, Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics), which does not accelerate local models.

steps.prompt: What is the capital city of Japan? Reply with the city name only.

steps.what: carries out multi-step arithmetic and reports the right result
steps.prompt: A train departs at 14:45 and the journey takes 2 hours and 40 minutes. At what time does it arrive? Reply with the time only, in 24-hour HH:MM format.

steps.what: solves a constraint puzzle rather than guessing
steps.prompt: Three boxes are labelled APPLES, ORANGES and MIXED. Every label is wrong. You may take one fruit from one box. Which box do you pick to work out all three labels? Reply with the single label you pick and nothing else.
steps.groundTruth: the only box that resolves all three labels is "MIXED"

steps.what: writes code that actually runs and returns the right value
steps.prompt: Write a JavaScript function named fib(n) that returns the nth Fibonacci number, where fib(0) = 0 and fib(1) = 1. Reply with only the function inside a single ```js code block. No explanation.
steps.groundTruth: the returned function, executed in a sandbox, must give fib(10) = 55

steps.groundTruth: the reply must parse as JSON with status "ok" and count 3

steps.what: warms the engine at the window the long request will need
steps.groundTruth: the runtime must accept a load-only request at num_ctx 8192

detail.note: This is the cost the user would otherwise pay AFTER pressing send.

steps.what: finds one planted fact in a long document
steps.prompt: 220-line log with the code on line 147 (20326 characters, ~5849 tokens, window 8192)
steps.groundTruth: reply must contain 742913, which appears exactly once in the document

detail.reason: The engine did not send anything back in time. A long document can take several minutes to read on this computer.
detail.notObservedHere: Node's fetch abandons a request whose first byte takes longer than 300 s. Measured directly against this engine with no such ceiling: 5,654 prompt tokens, 458.4 s of prompt evaluation at 12.3 tokens/second, 3.8 s of generation, and the correct answer. A browser has no 300 s ceiling and receives that answer; this harness cannot see it.

steps.what: reads a real image: printed digits and relative bar heights
steps.prompt: Two questions about this image. 1) What five-digit number is printed near the top? 2) Of the three dark bars along the bottom, is the tallest one on the left, in the middle, or on the right? Answer in one short sentence.
steps.reply: The five-digit number printed near the top is 58317, and the tallest bar among the three at the bottom is in the middle.
steps.groundTruth: the image (kept at release/artefacts/OCADE_CAPABILITY_VISION.png) shows 58317 and the middle bar is the tallest at 80px against 40px and 20px

steps.what: combines what it read in an image with a calculation
steps.prompt: Read the number printed in this image, then subtract 240 from it. Reply with exactly this JSON and nothing else: {"read":<the number in the image>,"result":<the subtraction>}

steps.what: stops immediately when the user stops it, and delivers nothing after
steps.groundTruth: no token may be delivered after the abort signal fires
